title: Chenin Blanc and Sémillon
subtitle: Two grapes, many styles
objectives: Describe Chenin Blanc's range in the Loire
Explain Sémillon's styles in Bordeaux and Australia

steps.title: Chenin Blanc
steps.body: Chenin Blanc has very high acidity and flavours of apple, quince and honey. In the Loire's Anjou and Touraine it makes every style: dry, off-dry, sweet and sparkling. Vouvray can be any of these; Savennières is dry and long-lived; Coteaux du Layon is sweet, often from noble rot. South Africa grows more Chenin than any other country.
steps.highlight: Chenin: high acid, dry to sweet

steps.title: Sémillon
steps.body: Sémillon has thin skins, low acidity and a waxy, lemony texture. Thin skins make it prone to noble rot, the fungus Botrytis cinerea, which shrivels berries and concentrates sugar. That's why it is the main grape of Sauternes. In Australia's Hunter Valley, picked early at about 10 to 11%, it makes lean whites that turn toasty and honeyed after ten years, without oak.

steps.prompt: Which styles can Chenin Blanc make in the Loire?
steps.explanation: Chenin is made dry, off-dry, sweet and sparkling in the Loire. Fortified wines aren't a Loire tradition.

steps.title: Blends and roles
steps.body: In Bordeaux, Sémillon is blended with Sauvignon Blanc: Sémillon gives body and texture, Sauvignon gives acidity and aroma. South Africa's Chenin often comes from old bush vines in Swartland and Stellenbosch, giving concentrated dry wines, sometimes oaked, that now rank among the country's best.
steps.highlight: Sémillon for body, Sauvignon for lift

steps.prompt: Why is Sémillon so suited to making Sauternes?
options: Its thin skins are prone to noble rot
steps.explanation: Thin skins let Botrytis cinerea attack, concentrating sugar. That's what makes Sauternes sweet.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Chenin Blanc makes dry, sweet and sparkling wines in the Loire
South Africa grows the most Chenin, often from old vines
Sémillon gives body, ages well in the Hunter and suits noble rot
